job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

response.passage: In a recent health awareness drive at a local community center, experts emphasized that invisible microbes, not just visible dirt, are the primary cause of illness. Many residents mistakenly believe that if hands look clean, they are free of pathogens, but germs are microscopic and thrive even on surfaces that appear spotless. Furthermore, the experts clarified that soap does not instantly kill all germs; instead, it works by lifting oils and pathogens off the skin so they can be rinsed away with water. To be effective, this process requires scrubbing for at least twenty seconds, as a quick five-second rinse is insufficient to remove stubborn microbes. Regarding water safety, the community learned that boiling water is the most reliable method to eliminate pathogens. Simply heating water until it starts to bubble is not enough; it must reach a rolling boil for several minutes to ensure all harmful organisms are destroyed. Finally, the health team addressed the misuse of medicines, stressing that antibiotics are designed specifically for bacterial infections and are completely ineffective against viral illnesses like the common cold or flu. Relying on antibiotics for viral symptoms only contributes to the global problem of drug resistance, making future infections harder to treat.
response.summary: This report explains that germs are invisible and require thorough handwashing with soap to be removed. It also highlights that boiling water properly is essential for safety and warns against using antibiotics for viral infections.
